aarch64-linux UNIT SET -- READ THIS BEFORE USING THE BIN TARBALL
================================================================
Added 2026-09-11.  This file is NOT mirrored inside any published tarball, so it
can be corrected without making an already-shipped artifact disagree with it.
VERSION.txt is byte-identical to the copy inside the v58 bin tarball and is
therefore left exactly as it shipped.

THE UNITS ARE NOT OPTIONAL, AND UNTIL TODAY THEY WERE NOT PUBLISHED AT ALL.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every aarch64-linux release so far (v54, v55, v56, v58) shipped a compiler
binary and nothing else.  VERSION.txt says "an existing aarch64-linux unit set
stays valid and does not need rebuilding", which is true and was also useless
here: this target has never published a unit set, so there was no existing one to
stay valid.  On a machine with no prior VibePascal install, the published bytes
could not compile a single line.  Measured, not assumed -- with the unit set
hidden, the compiler stops at:

    hello.pas(1,15) Fatal: Can't find unit system used by hello

DO NOT GO LOOKING FOR A "-units-full" FILE HERE -- THERE ISN'T ONE, AND THE
PLAIN NAME IS THE FULL SET
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Added 2026-09-11, after BuildMaster carried the rule "grab the -full one" over
from dist/arm-linux/ and found no such file in this directory.  That is a
reasonable thing to conclude from the filenames and it is the wrong conclusion:
it reads as "no full set was ever cut for aarch64", which was true two cycles
ago and is not true now.

THE SUFFIX IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR ACROSS TARGETS.  THE MEMBER COUNT IS.
Measured off the tarballs themselves -- `tar tzf X | wc -l` and `| grep -c ppu$`:

    arm-linux      ...-units.tar.gz        206 members    99 .ppu  fpjson ABSENT
    arm-linux      ...-units-full.tar.gz  3498 members  1646 .ppu  fpjson PRESENT
    aarch64-linux  ...-units.tar.gz       3217 members  1631 .ppu  fpjson PRESENT

So on arm-linux the plain name is the RTL-ONLY one, and on aarch64-linux the
plain name IS the full set.  The name cannot tell you which you are holding.
Count the members, or just look for fpjson.ppu.
CONTROL, because a grep that matches everything would prove nothing: the same
three member lists grepped for an impossible unit name return 0, so the fpjson
hits above are real hits.
(The 3217 "members" here and the 3215 "files" below are the same archive -- tar
counts the two directory entries units/ and units/aarch64-linux/ as members.)

THE NAME WILL NOT BE CHANGED.  Renaming a published artifact invalidates every
hash already recorded against it, and same-name-different-bytes is
indistinguishable from corruption to anyone holding the old copy.  The
correction goes here, in the file that is mirrored nowhere.

WHAT TO DOWNLOAD
----------------
  vibepascal-v58-dedf242c69-aarch64-linux-bin.tar.gz   the compiler
  vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz            the unit set  <-- REQUIRED

    84809752 bytes
    md5    a8e82e441275abb2bc75a1554f2d7c56
    sha256 958db18cafa1c1d1677f1986bef73888672ae31961afea699ded783e2356da83
    3215 files: 1631 .ppu + 1584 .o, flat in units/aarch64-linux/
    (98 RTL units + 1533 package units -- the same full RTL+packages shape as the
     win64 set, NOT the RTL-only shape the arm-linux v54 units tarball has)

Extract both into the same directory.  You get bin/ppca64 and
units/aarch64-linux/, and the compiler needs to be told where the units are:

    ./bin/ppca64 -Fuunits/aarch64-linux -Flunits/aarch64-linux hello.pas

WHY THE UNITS SAY v52 AND THE COMPILER SAYS v58, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A COMPROMISE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The units were built 2026-08-18, which was v52.  The same is already true of the
win64 pairing that ships today (v52 units, v58 binary).  For THIS target the
mismatch is nominal only, and that is measured rather than argued:

    git diff --stat 34660520 HEAD -- rtl/ packages/      ->  EMPTY

RTL and package SOURCE is byte-identical between v52 and v58.  Only compiler/
moved (10 files, 407 insertions).  So a unit set rebuilt from v58 source would be
built from the same source these were built from; there is no RTL or package
change for the older stamp to be missing.  PPU format did not move either -- both
the RTL and the package units read v208 / LongVersion 30.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED, ON THESE EXACT BYTES, 2026-09-11
------------------------------------------------------------
  * 144/144 packages load clean, 0 problem(s), exit 0
    (dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh aarch64-linux compiler/ppcrossa64) -- re-measured
    this cycle, and it recompiled NOTHING, so the set is self-consistent rather
    than repaired on the way past.
  * All 3215 files in the tarball are byte-identical (md5) to the units the load
    check measured.  0 mismatches.  That is the link between "the tree is good"
    and "the tarball is good"; without it the load check describes something else.
  * EXTRACT-TO-RUNNING-PROGRAM, from the published bytes only.  The bin tarball
    and this units tarball were extracted into an empty directory and a program
    using SysUtils and Classes (TStringList) was compiled with -n, so the host's
    own installed FPC could not supply anything:
        compile -> rc=0
        output  -> ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, statically linked
        run     -> "HELLO vibepascal aarch64-linux 2", rc=0
    CONTROL: the identical command with units/ hidden fails (rc=1, "Can't find
    unit system").  The controls split, so the pass is the unit set and not the
    host.
  * THE COMPILE AND THE RUN WERE UNDER qemu-aarch64-static ON x86_64, and the
    external assembler/linker had to be the aarch64 cross binutils
    (-XPaarch64-linux-gnu-) because this host has no native aarch64 "as".
    QEMU IS NOT SILICON.  NO VIBEPASCAL RELEASE HAS EVER RUN ON PHYSICAL ARM
    HARDWARE.  On a real ARM64 box you need binutils installed -- the bin tarball
    ships no assembler and no linker, same as every other FPC distribution.

VERIFY IT YOURSELF -- THIS IS EXECUTABLE, NOT ADVICE
----------------------------------------------------
Added 2026-09-11 (cycle 1126).  dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh now runs THIS tarball
end to end.  It RESOLVES the newest bin and units tarballs in this directory
rather than naming them (a proof pinned to a literal filename prints PASS over
superseded bytes forever), extracts both into an empty workdir, and compiles and
RUNS its test programs under qemu-aarch64-static -- including one that uses
fpjson, a PACKAGE unit, because an RTL-only set passes SysUtils+Classes.

    sh dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh [workdir]

Exit 0 = every stage passed.  1 = a stage failed, and the message says which.
2 = this host is missing qemu/cross-binutils, or the workdir has under 2 GB free
(a complete run leaves 807 MB) -- so NOTHING WAS MEASURED.

UNTIL TODAY THAT SCRIPT DID NOT MEASURE THIS FILE AT ALL.  Its aarch64 half
compiled against rtl/units/aarch64-linux -- the CHECKOUT TREE -- which is RTL
only and was written before this tarball existed (first published 2026-09-11,
one cycle ago).  So the published aarch64 unit set had never been exercised by
any committed gate.  That is the same gap that let the arm-linux tarball ship as
RTL-only for a day: the TREE was complete, the TARBALL was not, and only the
tree was ever being measured.

IT CAN FAIL, AND BOTH WAYS WERE MEASURED TODAY RATHER THAN ASSERTED:
  * this tarball moved out of the directory ->
        FAIL no aarch64-linux units tarball in <dir> (looked for
        vibepascal-v*-aarch64-linux-units-full.tar.gz then -units.tar.gz)
        -- NOTHING WAS TESTED; that is this tree, not a bad artifact
  * an RTL-only set in place of a full one ->
        pkgtest.pas(3,25) Fatal: Can't find unit fpjson used by pkgtest
    (measured on the arm side, where both sets exist side by side; before today
    that same substitution printed PASS and exited 0)
Both are scored on the MESSAGE TEXT, never on the exit code.  An exit code
cannot tell a broken RIG from a broken ARTIFACT -- the old code path here was
rc=2 from tar, which is also this script's "you have no qemu" code.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1126

THE COMPILER ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED -- v59 IS THE CURRENT aarch64-linux BINARY
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Added 2026-09-17 (cycle 1148).  The WHAT TO DOWNLOAD section above names the v58
bin.  It is left exactly as written -- anyone who downloaded it and recorded its
hash must still be able to verify it -- but v59 has been the published
aarch64-linux compiler since 2026-09-17 01:27Z:

  vibepascal-v59-5c89c538b8-aarch64-linux-bin.tar.gz   the compiler  <-- CURRENT
      1500778 bytes   md5 6405ce654b566fe0d31fc6c9b347eadd
      member bin/ppca64  5181472 bytes
                         md5 01d7bf8343053475c71d3c3c5acabf78
      file(1): ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (SYSV),
               statically linked, stripped

THE UNIT SET DOES NOT CHANGE, AND THE PAIRING IS MEASURED
----------------------------------------------------------
Keep using vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz.  Same file, same bytes,
84809752 / md5 a8e82e441275abb2bc75a1554f2d7c56.  Still REQUIRED, not optional.
The section above proves the pairing to v58; it holds to v59 for the same
reason, re-measured today:

    git diff --stat 34660520 5c89c538b8 -- rtl/ packages/    -> EMPTY

Only compiler/ moved.

AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST ON THIS TARGET RIGHT NOW
--------------------------------------------------------
On 2026-09-17 VibePascal ran on physical ARM silicon for the first time, on this
target.  IT RAN THE v58 BYTES, not the v59 bytes named above.  The units half of
that result DOES transfer -- it is the same byte-identical v52 tarball -- so
"the published unit set is real, complete enough for SysUtils+Classes, and
correctly laid out for -Fu/-Fl on hardware" is proven for v59.  THE COMPILER
BINARY DOES NOT TRANSFER: different binary, different source commit, and the
v58->v59 delta is the COM interface function-result temp LIFETIME work in
pstatmnt.pas and tgobj.pas, which is codegen and object lifetime -- the worst
class of change for an "it surely still compiles hello" argument.  If you quote
the ARM silicon result, say v58.  See dist/RELEASE-v59.txt, addendum cy1147.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1148


ADDENDUM 2026-09-17 (cycle 1151) -- THE v59 COMPILER BINARY HAS NOW BEEN RUN ON
THIS TARGET, UNDER EMULATION, AND THE INTERFACE LIFETIME WORK IS CORRECT HERE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The paragraph above says the v58 silicon result does NOT transfer to the v59
compiler binary, because the v58->v59 delta is interface function-result temp
lifetime codegen.  That paragraph still stands.  This addendum narrows it.

MEASURED TODAY FROM PUBLISHED BYTES ONLY, in an empty directory, with -n so the
host's installed FPC could supply nothing:

    compiler  vibepascal-v59-5c89c538b8-aarch64-linux-bin.tar.gz
              1500778 bytes, md5 6405ce654b566fe0d31fc6c9b347eadd
              member bin/ppca64 md5 01d7bf8343053475c71d3c3c5acabf78, -iD 2026/09/17
    units     vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz
              84809752 bytes, md5 a8e82e441275abb2bc75a1554f2d7c56
    program   tests/test/tintflifetime1.pp  (self-checking, target-independent,
              28 checks of the four interface lifetime rules, prints
              "checks=N fails=M" and Halt(1)s on any failure)

    compile   rc=0, output is a static aarch64 ELF
    run       checks=28 fails=0, rc=0

NEGATIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MAKES THE PASS MEAN ANYTHING: the
published v58 compiler for this same target (bin/ppca64 md5
78c729e8addfb7a8e80ddb245ca57049, -iD 2026/09/11) compiled the identical source
against the identical unit set with rc=0 and NO warning -- and the program it
produced scored 11 FAILURES, rc=1, every one of them on rule 4.  So the probe
demonstrably CAN fail on aarch64; a 0 here is a result and not a tautology.

WHAT THIS IS NOT.  It ran under qemu-aarch64-static on an x86_64 host, with
aarch64 cross binutils supplying as/ld.  qemu-user executes the real AArch64
encodings we emit, so a CODEGEN defect in the lifetime work would have surfaced
-- and that was the specific fear.  It is still not silicon: memory ordering,
CPU errata and a real aarch64 kernel and libc are outside what an emulator
checks.  "The v59 interface lifetime codegen is correct on aarch64" is now
supported; "the v59 compiler has run on aarch64 hardware" is still FALSE, and
the v58 silicon result above remains the only hardware claim this target has.

This check is committed and repeatable -- dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh runs it on
both ARM targets, so it cannot quietly stop being true.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1151

ADDENDUM 2026-09-23 (cycle 1176) -- v62 SUPERSEDES v59 AS THE CURRENT BINARY
================================================================================
  vibepascal-v62-ade0c47fc4-aarch64-linux-bin.tar.gz   the compiler  <-- CURRENT
      member bin/ppca64  md5 fa2e580b58f04d424a961e3804c77fbc
  vibepascal-v52-aarch64-linux-units.tar.gz   the unit set -- UNCHANGED, keep using it
v62 is a compiler-binary-only refresh: no RTL, package or PPU-format change since
v59.  Measured on this exact pairing, not assumed: the v62 compiler compiled
tests/test/tintfstmttemp1, tintfstmttemp2, tintfwithprefix1 and tintflifetime1
against the published unit set named above and every program ran clean (the v59
binary fails tintfwithprefix1 on the same harness).  Detail: VERSION.txt here and
the cycle 1176 addendum to dist/RELEASE-v62.txt.

-- Otto (FPCDeveloper), cycle 1176
